repo_notes.content:
opencode-sidebar is a VS Code extension that integrates the OpenCode AI tool (https://opencode.ai) as a persistent sidebar chat interface inside the editor. It is NOT a web app or a standalone CLI — it is a VS Code webview extension written in TypeScript.

Key architectural facts:
- The extension host (src/extension.ts, src/sidebar/, src/opencode/) runs in Node.js inside VS Code and manages the OpenCode server process lifecycle.
- The webview UI (src/webview/) is a vanilla-TypeScript component tree (no React/Vue) bundled separately by esbuild into dist/webview/main.js. It uses a Redux-style Store class for state management.
- Communication between the extension host and the webview uses VS Code's postMessage API with typed protocols defined in src/sidebar/bridgeProtocol.ts.
- Real-time AI responses arrive as Server-Sent Events (SSE) from the OpenCode server, handled by src/opencode/sseClient.ts.
- The OpenCode server is either spawned automatically via src/opencode/serverProcess.ts or attached to an existing running instance via the opencode.serverUrl setting.
- AI provider API keys (Anthropic, OpenAI, Google AI, Groq, Mistral, xAI, DeepSeek, Cohere) are managed through the VS Code secrets API and passed to the OpenCode CLI.

Build system: esbuild with two targets — a CommonJS bundle for the extension host and an ESM bundle for the webview. TypeScript strict mode. Vitest for unit tests. VS Code Test CLI for integration tests.
repo_notes.author: arielgoes

pages.title: Overview
pages.purpose: Explain what opencode-sidebar is, what problem it solves, and how it fits into a developer's workflow. Cover: what OpenCode is, why an IDE sidebar integration is useful, and a high-level feature list (multi-session chat, multi-model support, provider key management, streaming responses, tool call display, context usage tracking).

pages.title: Installation & Requirements
pages.purpose: Document how to install the extension. Cover: VS Code version requirement (1.118.0+), OpenCode binary prerequisite and where to get it, installing from a .vsix package step-by-step, and the planned marketplace publication.

pages.title: Configuration
pages.purpose: Document all VS Code settings contributed by the extension under the opencode.* namespace: binaryPath, serverArgs, defaultModel (provider/model format), and serverUrl. Include example values and explain when each setting is needed.

pages.title: Building from Source
pages.purpose: Step-by-step guide for contributors or users who want to build the .vsix themselves. Cover: prerequisites (Node.js 18+, npm, git), cloning, npm install, npm run compile vs npm run package, how to install the resulting .vsix, and how to launch the Extension Development Host with F5 for debugging.

pages.title: Architecture
pages.purpose: Technical deep-dive into how the extension is structured. Describe the three-layer architecture: (1) Extension Host — registers the webview provider, manages the OpenCode server process, bridges messages; (2) Webview UI — vanilla-TS component tree, Redux-style Store, renders sessions/messages/composer; (3) OpenCode Client — wraps @opencode-ai/sdk, handles REST + SSE. Include the data flow: user input → postMessage → extension host → OpenCode REST API → SSE stream → extension host → postMessage → webview render.

pages.title: Webview Components
pages.purpose: Document each UI component in src/webview/components/: Header (new session, restart server, manage keys buttons), SessionList (collapsible list with delete), MessageList (conversation display, empty state), Composer (textarea, send/stop, model picker), TextPart / ToolPart / PermissionPart (message content renderers), ModelPicker (provider+model dropdown). Explain the state flow through the Store.

pages.title: OpenCode Server Integration
pages.purpose: Explain how the extension integrates with the OpenCode server. Cover: auto-spawn via serverProcess.ts, attach to existing server via serverUrl, the SSE client with reconnection/backoff logic, the apiClient wrapping @opencode-ai/sdk for session and message management, and how provider API keys are passed to the CLI.

pages.title: Contributing & Testing
pages.purpose: Guide for contributors. Cover: development workflow commands (npm run watch, npm run lint, npm run check-types), unit tests with Vitest (npm run test:unit), extension integration tests with VS Code Test CLI (npm run test), and the dual-bundle esbuild setup in esbuild.js.
